lesson.title: Read the scale and the line
lesson.subtitle: P4 line-graph revision
lesson.objective: Read the scale of a line graph and read values from it.
lesson.story: A line graph shows books borrowed for Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri.

steps.title: Read the scale
steps.prompt: Look at the scale up the side. How many books borrowed does each gridline step stand for?
hints: Look at the numbers at the bottom and the top of the scale.
Count how many equal steps there are from the bottom to the top.
The scale reaches 50 in 5 equal steps, so work out 50 ÷ 5.

steps.title: Read a point
steps.prompt: How many books borrowed does the graph show for Tue?
hints: Find Tue along the bottom and follow it up to the point.
From the point, read across to the scale. Use the step size you found.
The point is 2 whole steps and a half step up the scale.

steps.title: Compare two points
steps.prompt: Which shows more books borrowed: Tue or Fri?
hints: A higher point means a bigger number.
Find both points and see which is higher on the graph.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why should you check the scale before reading a line graph?

choices.label: The scale is only there to decorate, so it does not change readings.
Every line graph scale goes up in ones, so you just count the steps.
A step on the scale can stand for more than 1, so check its size.

hints: Think about the numbers up the side.
Steps can stand for 5, 10 or 20, not always 1.
The size of a step changes every reading.
Choose the explanation about what each step stands for.
